sentences: The detective's daughter prepares to give birth to his first grandchild.
While the detective waits at the hospital, his "number two" son intercepts a message intended for the detective about a murder aboard the freighter.
The freighter is on its way from one port city to another port city under the command of the captain (an actor).
The older son, wanting to prove his investigative skills, boards the ship pretending to be his father, with his younger brother (an actor) in tow.

The ruse doesn't last long and soon the real detective arrives on board, interrogating a motley assortment of crooks, heiresses, and crew members as he works to solve a crime whose only witness is the secretary (an actress).

The suspects include the eccentric scholar (an actor), who claims to have kept a human brain alive in formaldehyde for six months and is always looking for new subjects; the divorcing woman (an actress), embroiled in a bitter divorce settlement involving $300,000 in stolen cash; and the criminal (an actor), who is being extradited to the home country in the custody of the escorting detective (an actor).
The captain is eager to unload his cargo, which is mostly a shipment of lions destined for a city zoo.
The deckhand is fond of walking his pet lion on the main deck, to nobody's pleasure.
The older son starts a fire on the ship, hoping to panic the killer in grabbing the hidden money and making a run for it.
The detective's anger is cooled when the older son shoves him out of the way of an assassin's bullet.
The detective recovers the gun and announces that the murderer will be revealed by the fingerprints on the gun.
The lights go out for a few moments, and now the gun is gone.
But while stealing the gun in darkness, the guilty party triggered an infra-red camera that identifies the culprit.
The story ends with the remaining passengers gathered around the ship-to-shore phone, listening to the coos and cries of the detective's first grandchild.

The aspiring actor has been relegated by the studio to the role of a "stooge" arranging publicity for the rising star, but when a photo shoot doesn't happen, the rising star winds up walking away from the manipulative studio boss.
The studio boss then assigns the aspiring actor to act as a stooge for the fading star.
In the meantime and in spite of the attentions of the studio publicity agent, the aspiring actor tries to pursue the actress, but she shows little interest in him.
Events lead the main characters to a party at a club, a desert resort with illegal gambling.
As a way of creating media interest, the aspiring actor stages a fake shooting.
Soon after, the studio boss advises the aspiring actor to get the fading star out of the club because of an impending police raid.
During the raid, however, the lights go out and someone shoots and kills the studio boss.
When suspicion falls on the aspiring actor, he and the publicity agent get away, eventually hopping on a train's flatbed car.

Thinking that they may know who the killer really is, the couple return to the fading star's home in the film district, where the prime suspects are gathered under the watchful eye of the police captain who expects the aspiring actor to return.
Ultimately, the captain performs paraffin tests on the suspects to see who else had recently fired a gun.
The fading star then confesses and is arrested.
Afterward, the aspiring actor and the publicity agent have coffee at a hamburger stand, considering leaving the movie business.
When the stand's owner expresses his frustration with his job, the aspiring actor offers to buy the stand, and he and the publicity agent look forward to a happier life.
At 3:00 am, the socialite takes her little dogs for a walk.
Near a subway construction site, she sees the fleeing man run out of a house and drive away.
The house is for sale by the seller, the wife of the victim, a wealthy banker.
Inside, the socialite finds a diamond brooch and the victim's dead body.
As she runs for help, her cloak falls off with the brooch inside it.
When the police arrive, the body, cloak, and brooch are gone.
The socialite and her friends are notorious pranksters, so the police lieutenant, does nothing to investigate the murder.
The newspaper editor writes an editorial decrying the socialite's "prank", and she sues him for libel.
The socialite and her friends decide they must find the murderer in order to defend their reputation.

The resulting manhunt includes searches of the victim's house, the fleeing man's apartment, the victim's business office, and all of the local beauty shops; two attempts to intimidate the socialite; two shooting attempts on her life: at a charity ball, and a trap set for the murderer using the socialite as bait.
The women twice attack the newspaper editor and tie him up, although the socialite's friend enthusiastically flirts with him.
Meanwhile, the socialite is approached by a woman who is now the girlfriend of the seller's ex-husband, a former convict, who has just finished a 10-year stretch at a prison.

She claims an alibi that she and the ex-husband were at a hockey game at the time of the murders and the ten minutes the ex-husband took for a smoke break at the intermission wasn't enough time for him to be at the scene of the crime.

While the police lieutenant repeatedly accuses innocent people based on incorrect theories, the socialite deduces that the fleeing man removed the body and cloak from the victim's house before the police arrived.
An escaping would-be killer leaves behind a piece of tar paper, which reminds the socialite of the subway construction site.
Returning to the site, she finds a fast electric cart on the track.
This is how the ex-husband made his way to and from the crime scene in ten minutes.
The ex-husband is captured after confessing to the murders and briefly holding the socialite and the newspaper editor hostage at gunpoint.
During the film, the relationship between the socialite and the newspaper editor evolves from sharp animosity to love and engagement.
He almost immediately decides that he is going to marry her and begins to woo her aggressively.
After the police rescue them from the ex-husband, the socialite and the newspaper editor plan their honeymoon.
After losing all his money gambling on horses, the former newspaper reporter and his companion break into a vacant mansion belonging to a wealthy family for shelter from the rain.
Just as the pair are settling in, the head servant and three other servants arrive.
The head servant, the butler, does not know what the long-absent, but expected publisher's son looks like, so he assumes that the reporter is him.
The reporter decides to impersonate the young publisher's son, the black sheep son of a wealthy big-city newspaper publisher, for a while when he learns the family will be away for weeks.

A neighbor develops an interest in the reporter, while a showgirl, wife of the real publisher's son (under an assumed name), shows up and tells him her husband is being framed for the murder of a political bigshot.
The reporter agrees to try to clear him in exchange for the showgirl not revealing his masquerade.
The reporter reluctantly accepts a job on the publisher's paper under an assumed name, and though the editor warns him not to play detective (a common tendency of new reporters), he does anyway.
He gets into trouble with the neighbor when he learns that her father, the judge, was with the victim the day he was killed.
He jumps to the conclusion that the judge is the killer, but the real murderer - the nightclub owner - is eventually caught (in spite of the reporter's efforts), and the publisher's son is released.
When the neighbor and her father are introduced to the publisher's son by his father, who has returned early, they wonder who the reporter really is.
Meanwhile, the reporter does his best to hide what has gone on and to present the publisher's son in the best light to his family.
The publisher's son's mother learns the truth from the publisher's son and the showgirl, but is pleased to conceal the story from her husband, who is very proud of his reformed son.
The editor lets the reporter keep his job and sends him to get the scoop on a rich widow's new husband, who turns out to be his companion.
The neighbor catches up with him and demands to know what is going on.
When the reporter tells her it would take a lifetime to explain, she replies, "Darling, that's just what I mean."

In a city, the police lieutenant (an actor) takes the investigator, a detective and the young man (an actor), a student, to a prizefight between the first boxer (an actor) and the second boxer (an actor), where the winner will take on the champion (an actor).
However, the fight is fixed and the gangster (an actor) bets big money that the second boxer won't make it to the fifth round.
He goes down in the fourth and dies shortly afterward.
The bookie (an actor) loses a fortune.
The investigator proves that it was murder and it is revealed that $100,000 was won in bets around the country against the second boxer.
The investigator works with the police lieutenant to solve the murder as the championship fight looms.
Comedy is provided by a comic character (an actor), a kleptomaniac, and the young man.
The investigator promised to reveal the murderer's identity on the night of the big fight, but the murderer has plans, too, with a concealed gun, to kill the investigator.
The husband's (an actor) private detective agency is not making any money, so he decides to swallow his pride and return to work for the district attorney as a special investigator.
His wife (an actress), who persuaded him to start his own business, decides to keep the agency going herself.
The wife is quickly hired by the client (an actress) to investigate the other woman (an actress), a former girlfriend of the client's husband (an actor) who has been in contact with him.

At a nightclub owned by the club owner (an actor), pretending to be out with the husband for pleasure rather than business, the wife witnesses the other woman's angry fiancé (an actor) threatening the client's husband, and before long the client's husband ends up dead.
The fiancé is the prime suspect.
A businessman (an actor), the fiancé's employer, talks him into hiring the wife to prove him innocent.
The club owner could be behind it, she figures, but his body is found in the couple's apartment, where the wife catches a whiff of a familiar perfume, the client's.

Escaping police custody as a murder suspect, the wife gets the client to sign a confession that she killed the club owner in self defense by pretending to have found her handkerchief at the scene of the crime.
However, the husband arrests the client for hiring the club owner to kill the client's husband to inherit all of his estate instead of getting a divorce settlement.
When the club owner started blackmailing her, she killed him.
A married couple, a husband and wife sleuthing duo, sell rare books in a big city and dream of taking a vacation to escape the sweltering heat of the city.
The husband decides to take the wife to a seaside resort town, where his friend is managing a beauty pageant.
In addition to his vacation plans, the husband, who has invested $5,000 in the pageant, plans to supervise the event's finances.
Soon after arriving in the seaside resort town, the husband discovers that the unscrupulous promoter of the pageant is duping the friend.
The wife is troubled to learn that the husband is a pageant judge and becomes jealous when he socializes with the contestants prior to the pageant.

The husband senses trouble when the big-city racketeer arrives to monitor the promoter's activities and when the promoter's publicity director lashes out at the rival contestant for vying with her for the promoter's attentions.
A detective tells the husband that the promoter will be arrested on swindling charges as soon as a warrant is issued.

When the promoter is mysteriously murdered, the friend is arrested and suspected of the crime because he had visited the promoter to demand all of the money owed to him and was last person seen with the promoter.
Although the husband and the wife are warned by the police chief not to involve themselves in the case, along with the help of the newspaper columnist they begin to investigate the murder.
Soon after, an attempt is made on their lives when a falling elevator nearly crushes them.
The husband does not believe that the friend was the murderer, but instead suspects the publicity director, because she and the promoter were involved in a dispute prior to the murder.

Later, when the husband discovers that the rival contestant smokes the same brand of cigarettes as the one found smoldering at the scene of the promoter's murder, he interrogates her and she names the racketeer as the murderer.
The racketeer, overhearing her accusation, attacks her and tells the husband that she is trying to frame him.
When the rival contestant is found murdered, the husband deduces that the murderer must be the columnist, because he is the only person who knew that he had proof against the rival contestant.
The husband tricks the columnist into confessing his guilt, but the columnist, in an attempt to silence the husband, tries to kill him.
However, he is prevented from doing so by the police, who arrest him.
Eventually, the husband learns that the columnist killed the promoter because the rival contestant threw him over for the promoter, and that he killed the rival contestant because she knew too much.
The retired safecracker, the famous thief, is kidnapped off a capital-city street and taken to a man whose face is hidden in darkness.
The mystery man offers the retired safecracker a job: breaking into a safe.
When the retired safecracker declines, he is released unharmed.
Afterward, a puzzled henchman states they can open the safe without help.
His boss reveals that he has "an old score to settle with the famous thief."
The plans for the inventor's new anti-aircraft gun are stolen from the war ministry and a cigarette deliberately left to incriminate the retired safecracker.
However, the thieves did not get all of the plans.
The inventor kept the key parts.

The police inspector knows the retired safecracker, one of the few capable of doing the job, is long retired and it is an obvious frameup, but is eager to seize any opportunity to try to jail him anyway.
The retired safecracker has an alibi though; he was having lunch with a blonde singer.
At home, the retired safecracker has woman trouble.
A widower, he tells his young daughter that he is sending her away to school, while his pretty heiress girlfriend is fuming because he left her at lunch to take a phone call and did not come back.
The police inspector and the sergeant question him, then leave.
At a bar, the retired safecracker meets the mysterious woman, much to the girlfriend's disgust.
The retired safecracker accompanies the mysterious woman and is forcibly taken to the inventor's laboratories to steal the rest of the plans.
He escapes, opens the safe, takes the plans from an envelope, replaces them with one for a baby carriage and reseals the envelope.
Then he allows himself to be recaptured.
He opens the safe and allows the spies to take the envelope.
They let him go, certain that the police will arrest him.
The retired safecracker entrusts the documents to the senator, the girlfriend's father, while he tries to clear himself.
He discovers that the mysterious woman is associated with a certain ringleader.
He crashes the ringleader's masquerade party, improvising a costume and stealing an invitation from a drunk.
He triggers the burglar alarm, then watches undetected as the ringleader, his vengeful nemesis, opens his concealed safe to check if his share of the plans is still there.
The retired safecracker then steals the plans, but is caught.
He runs into two policemen, brought by the drunk, and escapes.
When he gets home, he learns that the henchman has stolen his part of the plans from the senator.
With a tight deadline, the mysterious woman asks the retired safecracker to join forces with the ringleader, but is rejected.
The daughter sneaks into the trunk of the mysterious woman's car and is later discovered.
The retired safecracker goes after her to the ringleader's house and is captured with his half of the plans.
When the girlfriend is unable to convince the police inspector to accompany her to the ringleader's place, she goes there alone and is easily caught.
The police spot the retired safecracker's car at the ringleader's place and arrive in time to save everyone.
The detective arrives in the island to investigate the murder of an American agent, the dead agent, and uncovers a murderous smuggling ring.
On the ship taking him to the capital city, he unwillingly acquires the services of a dim-witted, but good-hearted professional wrestler the wrestler after he teaches him jujutsu.
Also travelling with the detective is the young woman, the daughter of the police commissioner the colonel.
Upon landing in the capital city, the detective is apparently ill with appendicitis.
The ambulance that is to take him to the hospital is hijacked by the smugglers led by the smuggler captain who plan to execute him, but the wrestler arrives in time to save him.
The detective was not ill as he claimed, and uses his jujutsu skills to defeat the would-be-assassins.
The detective claimed to need an appendicitis operation in order to find out who is the leader of the smuggling ring.

As only a few people around the governor, the governor of the island, knew that he had reported that he needed an appendicitis operation, he deduces that one of them must the leader of the smuggling ring.
Despite being old friends, there is much tension between the governor and the colonel over the latter's inability to solve the dead agent murder case or to discover who the diamond smugglers are.

Upon learning that the dead agent had taken out several books from the library concerning a famous-pirate-like pirate known as the pirate chief and his rumored hiding place in a nearby swamp, the detective decides that the diamond smugglers must be using the same swamp.
Present at the library is the wealthy shipper and friend of the governor, the businessman.
The detective and the wrestler are fired upon when they visit the swamp.
Upon the detective's return to the capital city, a hotel valet is killed when he tries to fill up the detective's bathtub, which has been rigged to electrocute whoever uses it.
Evidence emerges that the colonel is involved in the smuggling ring while the young woman overhears someone at the party talking on the phone to the smuggler captain.
Later at the same party, the governor is murdered and the colonel is found at the crime scene.
The police commissioner, the police chief, accuses the colonel of being the murderer, but the detective persuades the police chief to allow the colonel to return home.
The next day, the police chief, the detective and the wrestler go to the colonel's home and find that he and his daughter have disappeared.
The detective says that the colonel and his daughter have been kidnapped while the police chief believes they have fled, and orders the colonel's arrest.
A cable arrives saying that the detective is really the master criminal the notorious crook and the real detective is in a distant city.
The police chief then orders the arrest of the detective and the wrestler, accusing them of being the murderers, but the detective's jujutsu skills allows him and the wrestler to escape.
After hiding from the police, the detective tells the wrestler that he sent the cable himself in order to infiltrate the smuggling gang who have kidnapped the young woman.
After infiltrating the gang in their camp in the swamp, the detective finds the colonel and his daughter have indeed been kidnapped.
The detective is exposed as a double agent when the smuggler captain arrives at the camp, but he is able to escape with the wrestler.
The detective contacts the police chief and reveals his ruse.
The detective leads the police on a raid and they pursue the smuggler captain fleeing with the young woman on his boat.
Despite the detective's orders to take the smuggler captain alive, the businessman shoots the smuggler captain.
The detective has the smuggler captain taken to the hospital and announces that based on what the doctors have told him, the smuggler captain will reveal who his boss is at 8 pm.
Just before 8 pm, the smuggler captain is stabbed.
The detective reveals that the colonel has been framed and the leader of the gang is the businessman who is caught throwing the knife into the smuggler captain.

The detective states that the smuggler captain was not wounded, but killed by the businessman earlier that day, and he maintained the deception of the smuggler captain still being alive to force the businessman to reveal himself.
With the businessman arrested, the young woman declares her love for the young man, the governor's son, while the wrestler thanks the detective for teaching him jujutsu.
The detective tactfully tells the wrestler his services will not be needed on his next case and demonstrates that the wrestler still has much to learn about jujutsu.
The father sues his ex-wife the mother for the custody of their son.
The owner of the detective agency, where the investigator works, asks her to testify against the mother.
The investigator refuses because the father only wants the custody of his son to have access to the child's trust fund.
When her boss insist that she testify, the investigator decides to quit her job and marry her boyfriend, police lieutenant the lieutenant.
The lieutenant is thrilled when the investigator arrives at the police station and wishes to be married that night.
However, the investigator is distracted when she overhears an incoming call from the father, demanding police protection because the mother has threatened his life.
This was a scheme concocted by his lawyer, the lawyer, who kills the father in his home later that night.
The mother is seen leaving his house just as the gunshot is heard by a neighbor.
The investigator tags along as the lieutenant and his assistant the assistant investigate the crime.
She finds the mother hiding in a hotel and tells her that the police suspect her fiancé, the fiancé.
The mother lies and says she is the killer.
The investigator believes the mother is innocent and helps her escape.
Meanwhile, the lawyer is trying to persuade the fiancé to turn the mother in and also hire him as her defense lawyer.
The lieutenant and the assistant arrive at the fiancé's home.
They have a confrontation with the fiancé and he escapes.
The investigator decides to help both the mother and the fiancé.
She questions the lawyer the next morning and learns that he has appointed himself the legal guardian of the mother's son.
The lieutenant is not happy with the investigator's interference in the case.
The investigator later finds evidence confirming the lawyer's guilt in his office.
She writes a report saying that the lawyer killed the father and framed the mother in order to get her son's trust fund.
As she is telling the lieutenant on the telephone to meet her at the office, the lawyer arrives and knocks the investigator unconscious and takes her to his beach house.
He is met by his partner the father's chauffeur, the chauffeur.
While the unconscious investigator is placed in a car in the garage, the mother and the fiancé arrive to give the lawyer a retainer to defend them.
The lieutenant and the assistant burst in, just when the chauffeur is about to give the mother and the fiancé poisoned drinks.
They had found the investigator's report about the lawyer in his office, and rescue the investigator before she becomes asphyxiated in the car.
After a struggle, they successfully capture the lawyer and the chauffeur.
